🇲🇽🔬 <u>Mexico's 2027 budget bets on science — up 18% in real terms</u>

The 2027 economic package earmarks 193 billion pesos for science, technology and innovation — an 18% real increase, per El Economista, with the science ministry's own budget up 13%. Education, science and culture together climb to 1.4 trillion pesos, 3.5% of GDP, and all of it with no new taxes and no new debt. After decades of neoliberal austerity starved Mexican science, the money is going back in.

🎶🇲🇽 <u>The Zócalo goes free for the 15th — Intocable headlines Independence</u>

Sheinbaum confirmed norteño legends Intocable will play a free concert in the Zócalo on September 15, the eve of the Grito de Independencia, for thousands of Mexican families. A Tejano-rooted band beloved on both sides of the border, headlining the nation's main square at no charge — the 4T's tradition of filling Mexico's most symbolic plaza with free culture for the people, not a ticketed spectacle.
banner: INTOCABLE FREE AT ZOCALO ON SEPT 15

🚨🇲🇽 <u>A third mayor cuffed in days — and this one's from Morena</u>

Federal and state forces arrested Isaac Rodríguez Ochoa, the Morena mayor of Esperanza, Puebla, along with his brother and his former police chief, for shielding the "Los Zúñiga" cargo-theft ring on the Puebla–Veracruz highway. Twenty-three raids turned up 35 guns — two of them Barrett rifles — plus a drone and a signal jammer. It's the third sitting mayor jailed in days, and the government didn't spare its own party to do it.
banner: PUEBLA: MORENA MAYOR JAILED IN THEFT RING

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Vulcan wanted $1.7 billion from Mexico — the tribunal said no</u>

US mining giant Vulcan Materials gouged limestone out of Calica, Quintana Roo, far beyond its permits — so Mexico turned the wrecked site into a protected natural area, and Vulcan ran to an ICSID tribunal demanding $1.7 billion. The panel just ruled the payout should be "considerably lower." Sheinbaum framed the fight plainly: "They want to take out the material they already dug up. What we want is the remediation of that place."

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>US–Iran clashes push oil past $100 — the peso barely blinks</u>

Attacks between the US and Iran shoved Brent crude back over $100 a barrel on Wednesday, its first time since July — yet the peso strengthened to 16.88 per dollar, near its best level of the year. Mexico's inflation held at a controlled 3.26% and Hacienda's 2027 budget landed with no new debt. Washington's wars rattle the markets; the Mexican economy keeps its footing.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>Sheinbaum draws the line: sovereignty is off the table</u>

Mexico opens tariff talks with Trump's commerce secretary Howard Lutnick this week, and Sheinbaum set the limit before sitting down: "we won't sign anything that affects our sovereignty or our economy." She's pressing Washington to drop its tariffs on Mexican steel, aluminum and autos — and rejecting any new ones. When the US tried to split the T-MEC partners into separate rooms instead of a trilateral table, Mexico kept its own direct line. Better conditions, yes; the well-being of the Mexican people traded away, never.
banner: MEXICO: NO DEAL THAT CEDES SOVEREIGNTY

🇲🇽📉 <u>Mexican Inflation Holds Near Banxico's 3% Target</u>

Mexico's annual headline inflation came in at 3.26% in its latest reading, with core inflation rising just 0.08% for the fortnight — below the 0.14% markets expected, El Economista reports from INEGI data. The number held near Banxico's 3% target even with onion up 19% and eggs up nearly 8%.

🇲🇽⚽ <u>Mexico City Bids to Be the World Capital of Sports Tourism</u>

Mexico City drew over 9 million hotel guests in the first half of 2026 — up 7% — while major events generated 60 billion pesos in economic impact and the sector grew 28% in a year, the city reported at the 4th World Sports Tourism Congress. More than 12 million people joined public activities during the World Cup, and the F1 Grand Prix is next on the calendar.

🇲🇽🕊️ <u>Homicides Down 53% — Lowest August in 12 Years</u>

Daily homicides in Mexico fell from 86.9 to 40.8 between September 2024 and August 2026 — a 53% drop, and the lowest August in a 12-year series, per the SESNSP. The homicide rate per 100,000 fell 49%, violent vehicle theft dropped 54%, and 30 of 32 states improved, led by San Luis Potosí at −80%. "El promedio de 40.8 homicidios diarios es el menor observado," said security official Marcela Figueroa.

🇲🇽📚 <u>Mexico Holds Steady on PISA as the OECD Slides</u>

While the OECD average fell 22 points in math and 28 in reading over the decade, Mexico held its ground in reading and science on PISA 2025 — after expanding coverage to more vulnerable students without widening the gap. Even the OECD's own Andreas Schleicher conceded: "México ha mostrado resiliencia."
